decisive_items: A skin biopsy revealed numerous dermal ectatic blood vessels and lymphatics with a sparse lymphocytic infiltrate
non-erythematous, non-pitting edema of the left periorbital region
Paranasal radiography and maxillofacial CT scans showed only periorbital soft-tissue swelling
response.rationale: Chronic non-inflammatory periorbital edema in a young adult with biopsy showing dermal vascular/lymphatic ectasia and sparse lymphocytic infiltrate is most consistent with blepharochalasis. Lymphangioma is the closest differential but typically presents as a congenital cystic/orbital mass rather than isolated non-pitting eyelid edema with negative imaging findings.

rejected.why: Angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia requires eosinophilic inflammation and epithelioid vascular proliferation, not sparse lymphocytic infiltrate with ectatic vessels.
Orbital pseudotumor would show orbital inflammatory changes, pain, proptosis, or visual symptoms, which are absent.
Kimura disease has dense eosinophilic infiltration, elevated IgE, and often lymphadenopathy, none of which are present.
Lymphoma requires an atypical dense lymphocytic infiltrate and usually an identifiable orbital or systemic mass.
Sjögren's syndrome causes sicca and glandular inflammation, not isolated unilateral eyelid edema with ectatic lymphatics.
Orbital lymphoma would show an orbital mass or atypical lymphoid proliferation, not only periorbital soft-tissue swelling with sparse lymphocytes.
Sarcoidosis requires granulomatous inflammation, which is absent; tuberculin test was negative.
Angioedema is acute/transient and would show dermal edema rather than dilated blood vessels and lymphatics with an 8-month persistent course.
